attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalised proposition matches the plain present-tense claim. There are no conditions or horizon to keep.

contract.note: Reading the claim as 'lacking dependable learned rules that transfer to substantially unfamiliar cases' is an ordinary contextual reading. It does not demand total absence of abstraction. A 2024 window for the current state is reasonable.

evidence.note: June 2024 ARC verification scores: frontier LLM baselines got 4.5–14% on novel abstraction tasks. The 43% system used program generation and execution, which the contract says to separate from neural-only methods, so it does not rebut the claim.
The research was first reported in 2023 and shows variable, not robust, in-context generalization. It is background, not decisive for the 2024 window.

reviews.rationale: Leading neural LLMs scored very low on ARC's unfamiliar abstraction tasks in mid-2024. That fits the plain reading that they lack a good way to acquire general, transferable rules. The best result came from a hybrid program-execution approach, not neural-only methods. Nothing in the packet meets the contradiction condition. The support rests mostly on one benchmark, so it is limited in breadth.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, stated emphatically in his own voice.

semantics.note: Here 'will fail' describes a general mechanism, not a dated future event. The 'far enough from training examples' qualifier is kept.

contract.note: The contract reads this as an empirical claim about failures under distribution shift and requires outliers to be defined independently. That is fair. 'Far enough' and 'fail' have no thresholds, so interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Controlled in-domain vs out-of-domain splits on GPT-3/GPT-4 tasks show accuracy dropping sharply outside the trained region, with matched baselines. This is direct evidence that the shift causes the failure.
The reversal-curse failure is reproducible across model families and sizes, showing limited generalization beyond trained patterns.
May 2024: special embeddings allow extrapolation to 6x the trained length. This narrows any unrestricted reading but does not show success at an independently defined 'far enough' distance.

reviews.rationale: Controlled experiments show contemporary generative models degrade sharply on out-of-distribution splits compared with matched in-distribution baselines, which meets the support condition. The length-extrapolation result only narrows where the failure boundary sits. It does not rebut failure 'far enough' out. The universal inevitability reading is not proven, but the contract does not require that.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, in his own voice.

semantics.note: The revision restored 'Achilles' heel' and 'over a quarter century later'. The proposition is faithful.

contract.note: Reading 'Achilles' heel' as a major recurring weakness, and outliers as distribution shift following his own parenthetical, is ordinary and fair.

evidence.note: February 2024 evaluation: multimodal LLMs struggle beyond common training domains across synthetic, real-world, medical and molecular shifts. In-context learning helps but stays vulnerable to shifts.
Research from 2023, revised June 2024, finds a severe out-of-distribution robustness problem. Treated as background to the target window.

reviews.rationale: A 2024 primary evaluation found substantial, recurring failures under several kinds of distribution shift in contemporary neural systems, which meets the support condition. Gains from in-context learning are partial and remain vulnerable to shift, so they do not show reliable robustness. The contradiction condition is not met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps both halves of the contrast and the 30-year span. It slightly softens 'always' and 'a constant'.

contract.note: Reading the claim as a persistent contrast rather than literal perfection is generous and fair. Because he said 'always' and 'a constant', a clear counterexample of neural systematic generalization is fair to count against him.

evidence.note: 2020 gSCAN benchmark: neural models fail dramatically on novel compositions. This supports recurring neural difficulty within the window.

2023 Nature study: a meta-trained neural network achieved human-like systematic generalization, while symbolic models were systematic but rigid. This undercuts the constant contrast, although ordinary networks there were still unsystematic.
February 1994: a symbolic learner beat neural models on unseen verbs. This predates the August 1994 window, so it is background only.

reviews.rationale: The part that holds: neural networks have repeatedly struggled with novel cases (e6, and the ordinary networks in e7). The part that does not: by 2023 a specially meta-trained neural network achieved systematic generalization, and the symbolic comparators showed rigidity. So the contrast was not 'a constant' across the 30 years. The evidence for symbolic performance across the period is thin.
